races.title: State Assembly, District 75
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Carl DeMaio
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 75 since December 2024. Served on the San Diego City Council from 2008 to 2012. Founded the Performance Institute and the American Strategic Management Institute, and chairs Reform California. Hosts a podcast and formerly a KOGO radio show.

controversies.text: In 2014, two former campaign staffers accused DeMaio of sexual misconduct. He denied it. The San Diego DA declined to file charges, saying there was not enough evidence. In 2015 accuser Todd Bosnich pleaded guilty to obstruction for lying to the FBI about a threatening email. Prosecutors did not decide whether the harassment claims were true.

In October 2024, Rancho Bernardo neighbors Mohammad and Roya Zamanian sought a restraining order against DeMaio and his husband, alleging harassment over their landscaping. On Nov. 19, 2024, a judge denied the request in its entirety after a hearing. A DeMaio spokeswoman said he lives in Fallbrook, inside the 75th District.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California and Reform California (the organization DeMaio chairs) are listed as 2026 endorsers, along with several conservative voter-guide groups.
Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association endorsed him in 2012 and 2014, and he cited its endorsement in 2024.

cands.gaps: The pages we had showed no documented stance by DeMaio on data centers, on limiting investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, or on growth limits and land conservation. They also showed no bills or actions in office tied to the topics voters ask about, because the sponsored-legislation list on his profile was empty. His positions on gun laws are only partly documented: he has said he favors full enforcement of existing laws and a national concealed-carry permit program with background checks, but nothing on red-flag laws, purchase-age limits or suppressors. His education plans mention school choice and charters but not teacher pay. We could not independently confirm his upbringing details beyond a single encyclopedia account, and we found no news reporting on the 2024 neighbor dispute or residency question beyond that account.

local.label: Roots 80: Born in Dubuque, Iowa, he moved with his family to Orange County, California in the late 1970s and attended school in Anaheim through eighth grade, then left for boarding school in Maryland and college in Washington, D.C. before returning to San Diego in 2002.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Current Assemblymember (since 2024) and San Diego City Councilman (2008-2012), where he was vice chair of the Budget and Finance Committee. Founded and sold two government-performance and budget-training companies, worked as Director of Planning at the Congressional Institute (1994-99), and authored San Diego's 2012 pension reform ballot measure.
qual.why: Prior legislative service at the city and state levels, combined with a career in budget and government-management policy, fits the high band for writing law and the state budget.
qual.label: Prior legislative service at the city and state levels, combined with a career in budget and government-management policy, fits the high band for writing law and the state budget.

workers-first.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said he would repeal the Sanctuary State law that shields criminals from deportation and stop taxpayer-funded welfare for illegal immigrants.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2024 survey he said he supports fully funding public safety budgets and backing Prop 36. He said he authored a citizens' initiative to guarantee police and firefighters death and disability benefits.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His 2020 campaign site said he supports expanding parental choice and charter schools so all parents can make a real choice for their children's education. It did not mention teacher pay.

clean-money.evidence: In his 2024 survey he said he was running without special-interest support and relied on small contributions from grassroots supporters.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His 2020 campaign site said he opposes new tax hikes, including property tax proposals, and backs rolling back gas and car taxes. It did not specifically propose eliminating homestead property taxes.

prio.label: Matches 5 of 5 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 5 only promised

roots.summary: Born in Dubuque, Iowa, he moved with his family to Orange County, California in the late 1970s and attended school in Anaheim through eighth grade, then left for boarding school in Maryland and college in Washington, D.C. before returning to San Diego in 2002.

cands.name: Gerald C. Boursiquot
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California Assembly District 75. IT professional and U.S. Air Force veteran (2008–2023). Former union auto worker, according to his campaign. Has not held elected office. Advanced from the June 2026 primary against Assemblymember Carl DeMaio.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Young Democrats and Equality California, per Ballotpedia.
Congressman Mike Levin, San Diego Councilmember Marni Von Wilpert, La Mesa Vice-Mayor Lauren Cazares and several local Democratic clubs, as listed in his Ballotpedia survey response.

cands.gaps: He has never held office, so there is no voting record or legislative actions to report. We found no statements from him on data centers, institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, policing, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site gives no detail on property-tax policy beyond general tax relief. We could not independently confirm his birthplace, military service or employment history beyond his own survey answers and campaign site. We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable news coverage about him.

local.label: Roots 40: He says he was raised in Spring Valley, NY and has lived in North County San Diego since 2014, about 12 years, as an adult.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: 22-year Air Force veteran (Ballotpedia lists 2008–2023) and IT professional. His campaign site says he is a former union auto worker. He has held no elected office and lists no legislative, policy or budget career.
qual.why: He has real work experience in the military and IT but no legislative, policy or budget work and no local elected office, so he falls in the low-to-middle range for writing law and budgets.
qual.label: He has real work experience in the military and IT but no legislative, policy or budget work and no local elected office, so he falls in the low-to-middle range for writing law and budgets.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he would remove red tape to make permitting easier for affordable housing developers and incentivize multi-family housing development. It also says he would incentivize local governments to build while preserving North and East County's charm and character.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he would expand tax relief for veterans, unhoused people and working families through changes to the tax code. It names no homestead or property-tax proposal, so this is a loose match at best.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he would protect working families' right to organize for fair wages and working conditions. He states no position on H-1B or immigration enforcement, so this match is weak.

clean-money.evidence: He says he would redirect state funding from corporate subsidies to direct supports such as housing credits, job training and childcare subsidies. This is a stance on subsidies, not a pledge on donations.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 4 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

roots.summary: He says he was raised in Spring Valley, NY and has lived in North County San Diego since 2014, about 12 years, as an adult.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: He supports 'reasonable development policies' to grow the local economy, bringing job centers to North and East County, and streamlined permitting. He also supports affordable and multi-family housing development while preserving the region's 'charm and character.'
